title: Base-change comparison for the bounded proper flat model
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a scheme morphism, $F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-derived-direct-image], and $U$ an open of $T$. Let $C,D$ be cochain complexes of $\mathcal O_U$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], strictly zero above natural degrees $b,d$ respectively, with all terms flat over the identity of $U$ [def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Suppose $D$ is strictly zero below zero, and a quasi-isomorphism $e:C\to D$ is supplied. Suppose every cartesian base change $X'\to X$ over $T'\to U\to T$, with injective resolutions in $X'.\mathrm{Modules}$, identifies $H^q(g^*D)$ with $R^q f'_*(g'^*F)$ for every natural $q$ [def-pc-base-change, def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Then every pullback $g^*C$ has zero negative homology, and in every such cartesian square its nonnegative homology is isomorphic to $R^q f'_*(g'^*F)$.

proof.text: Convert flatness over the identity to tensor-exact sheaf flatness and apply bounded-above flatness to make both C and D K-flat.

Identify tensor pullback with ordinary pullback by uniqueness of left adjoints. Apply preservation of quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes and transport along the resulting natural arrow isomorphism.

For i < 0, the i-th term of D is zero, so its ordinary pullback has zero i-th homology. Transport along the homology isomorphism induced by the pulled-back e. For natural q compose that isomorphism with the supplied comparison for D. These are Mathlib isoOfQuasiIsoAt and ShortComplex.isZero_homology_of_isZero_X2.

statement_change.old_statement: For a bounded termwise flat quasi-coherent finitely presented model produced by the proper direct-image construction, negative homology vanishes after pullback and nonnegative homology identifies with higher direct images.
statement_change.what: The old signature quantified over an arbitrary bounded flat finitely presented complex without identifying it with a cohomology model. A nonzero finite free module in degree -1 contradicts the negative clause; the zero complex contradicts degree zero for f=id and F=O. Require a quasi-isomorphism to an actual nonnegative model, and prove transport. The caller must construct the model and its comparison together.

citers.note: The unchanged bounded-model existence statement is proved by a Cech model, a perfect replacement mapping to that model, and this transport theorem; its proof and imports are adapted in this delivery.
